chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abu al-Fadl al-Thaqafi from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a woman whose husband died while she was in her waiting period (iddah); he said: 'She performs Hajj, even if she is in her waiting period.'

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا: A woman whose husband has died

ai.seo_question: Can a widow perform Hajj while in her waiting period (iddah) after her husband's death?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a widow obligated to perform Hajj al-Fadilah or Hajj al-Ibadah may do so during her three-month waiting period (iddah) following her husband's death. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, where the ritual purity and presence required for Hajj are not hindered by the temporary state of mourning, provided the widow is not in the final stages of childbirth or menstruation which might require specific precautions. The hadith underscores the principle that personal religious obligations can be fulfilled concurrently with marital status changes, reinforcing the practical ease Islam places on believers.
